prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form that made possible incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: After reading the full first round, my scientific case for B046 is unchanged and rests on the arc, not on the unanimous opening ballots. Holst established GLP-1 secretion and insulinotropic action in humans, Drucker defined proglucagon-derived peptide biology, receptor action and the therapeutic rationale, and Mojsov identified and synthesised the active truncated peptide. Large randomized trials of the resulting drugs then showed benefit in glycaemia, weight, cardiovascular and renal endpoints. The mechanism has been confirmed independently for decades, so maturity is not in doubt and the discovery is neither premature nor contested on the science. The citation should name the physiology and the active form and refer to the therapies as the consequence, without naming any product. The chair's questions on scope do not change this. A citation that names the discovery is the most defensible scope for a prize that honours a discovery.
statement.case_against: The attribution remains the weak point, and round 1 did not resolve it. Nobody, including me, can settle from the supplied text whether Mojsov or Habener has the stronger claim to the active GLP-1(7-36) form. Habener is outside the credited names. Knudsen's work on liraglutide and semaglutide is where much of the patient impact originates, and the three-person cap forces a real choice. A physiology-led trio can be read as honouring the hormone biology while leaving out the drug design. Awarding it also turns an unresolved priority question into a public verdict. Long-term safety for obesity indications is still accumulating. I treat that as data still arriving, not as a reason to delay or reword the citation.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius argues that a one-part GLP-1 prize leaves CAR-T (B028), the other candidate with a clear bench-to-bedside arc, unrewarded, and asks whether a two-part prize is preferable, noting that Eshhar is outside the credit and Rosenberg's work is broader than CARs.
responses.response: I agree that CAR-T is the strongest second achievement. A year in which it goes unrecognised is a cost, but that cost is not a reason to build a prize now. The three-person cap makes the pairing concrete. Pairing B046 with B028 would leave me one name for one part, or two names for the other. That would mean dropping Mojsov or Holst from B046, or crediting only one of June, Sadelain and Rosenberg for CAR-T, and I cannot defend either on the supplied evidence. The Eshhar omission and your point that Rosenberg's contribution is broader than CARs make the B028 allocation harder than B046's. I therefore keep B046 as a single part and keep B028 as my first alternative. I would reconsider only if the committee agrees on a CAR-T allocation that is cleaner than the one we have.

responses.point: The chair moved from Knudsen to Mojsov in the third slot, reasoning that the cap forces a choice and that colleagues put the physiological and peptide-identification contributions ahead of analogue development. He still flags that the Mojsov priority is contested and that Knudsen is left unrecognised.
responses.response: I note that your move brings you to the configuration I held in round 1. That does not make the Mojsov question easier. My own reasoning is that the committee tradition favours the discovery of the biological principle, and Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the active peptide is what made the physiology testable and the drug design possible. Your point that a prize with Knudsen risks crowding out a basic discoverer is the one I find strongest. Drucker and Holst are both needed for the physiology, so a Knudsen award would displace the one name whose claim is least settled, and that is Mojsov. The case against Knudsen is therefore not about merit. A physiology citation cannot honour her work without naming a product, and I do not want the citation to do that. If the committee concludes the priority record is too unclear to credit Mojsov, I would want Knudsen in her place and the citation changed to the long-acting drugs. I do not think the supplied evidence reaches that point.

responses.point: Sandberg says that if the committee wants to honour the drug rather than the physiology, his trio is the wrong one, and that a prize omitting the industrial development may look incomplete to the public.
responses.response: I agree with the conditional, and it is the crux of the chair's first question. I land on the physiology side for a reason that does not depend on public perception. The hormone's biology is what remains valid whatever happens to individual products, and several drugs and combinations have been built on it. A prize for the biology therefore covers the whole class. A prize for liraglutide and semaglutide would honour one lineage of that class. The public optics are a real cost, but I would accept it. I would also reject using optics to add a fourth name, because the cap exists to force exactly this kind of choice. In round 1 I called your SMN2 antisense candidate the strongest therapeutic alternative on clarity. I still do, and I still rank it behind B046 for the reasons I gave.

responses.point: Perlmann ranks cGAS-STING (B029) as an alternative and also warns that awarding this prominent GLP-1 prize risks turning an unresolved priority dispute into a public verdict.
responses.response: Your warning about the public verdict is the point I find hardest to answer, and I take it seriously. I disagree only in part. Declining to credit a contested name is also a verdict, since it states that someone else's claim was stronger. The honest course is to credit on what the published record clearly supports and state that in the citation. A citation for the physiology and the active form does that. On cGAS-STING, my view is the same as before. The Chen and Barber mechanism is clean, but you yourself concede that no approved therapy exists yet. The question of Ishikawa's and Vance's roles is also open. It is a strong candidate for a later year. It does not outweigh a candidate with proven outcomes and decades of independent confirmation.

responses.point: Linnarsson names CAR-T as the next most robust candidate if the committee judges the Mojsov priority cannot be settled, and notes that six-way optogenetics credit would need to be reduced to three.
responses.response: I accept the conditional: if the priority record cannot support Mojsov, the right response is to revisit the allocation within B046, not to substitute another achievement. Moving to CAR-T because of one contested name would conflate two different questions. On optogenetics, my round-1 view stands, and I will not let my own field push it upward. I called the Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann set the clearest three, but that choice leaves out Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck, so the six-way credit is a real obstacle. The method also has only beginning clinical use. B038 stays as an alternative and nothing more.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov or Habener has the stronger documented claim to the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide. I cannot settle this from the supplied text, and if the record turned against Mojsov I would move Knudsen into her place.
Whether the committee will take the physiology of the hormone or the long-acting drug development as the essential achievement, since this decides whether the trio is right or incomplete.
Whether a second achievement could be added without cutting a B046 name below what the physiology needs. At present no pairing under the three-person cap seems defensible to me.
Long-term safety and effects of GLP-1 agonists in obesity indications are still accumulating, which may affect later commentary but does not change my citation.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal ground for B046 or any shortlisted ballot. My disclosures are unchanged. I co-authored a 2009 paper with Thomas Perlmann and a 2019 review with Sten Grillner, and neither is a credited candidate. I use optogenetics as a research field but have no documented involvement with the B038 candidates, so I disclose this only for transparency. Nothing in round 1 or the chair's summary adds a new disclosure.
